result.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. Realizing the benefits of these harnesses depends on how effectively the underlying model can make use of them, motivating reinforcement learning directly through the harness. However, existing approaches typically train through a single fixed harness, which can lead to specialization and limited transfer across harness configurations. To address this, we introduce \textbf{Harness Scaling}, a new scaling dimension for agentic RL that extends training from a single harness to diverse execution configurations. Concretely, we construct a factorized harness space, select a compact training subset with balanced factorial coverage, and organize cross-harness training to combine global coverage with controlled variation for the same task. Across multiple benchmarks, model scales, and RL algorithms, Harness Scaling consistently improves generalization to unseen white-box configurations. Moreover, models trained through structured white-box variation transfer effectively to unseen external black-box harnesses, outperforming models trained through a single complex black-box harness. These results establish harness diversity as a meaningful scaling dimension for agentic RL and highlight the importance of how this diversity is organized for cross-harness generalization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Harness Scaling，将 agentic RL 的训练从单一 harness 扩展到因子化的 harness 配置空间，并以均衡因子覆盖和受控变化组织跨 harness 训练，从而提升对未见配置及黑盒 harness 的泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「因子化配置空间＋均衡覆盖」的训练多样性组织方式，可能可供核查 LVR 中跨推理脚手架与轨迹形式的监督组织和长度泛化设计；但原文不涉及视觉证据或 latent 状态本身。
